# Purpose

This document demonstrates Quarto features intended for Microsoft Word
(`.docx`) output.

It intentionally does **not** use Jupyter, notebooks, or Python execution.

The document contains:

- two different tables;
- three different code-block approaches;
- five Mermaid diagrams;
- Mermaid diagrams configured to render as graphical figures rather than
  appearing as Mermaid source code in the final document.

# Code Blocks

## Option 1 — Plain Text

The simplest option is a normal fenced code block.

```text
TestExecution
  |
  +-- Initialize
  |
  +-- Execute tests
  |
  +-- Collect results
  |
  +-- Generate report
```

This option requires no syntax highlighting and is highly portable to DOCX.

## Option 2 — Language-Specific Code

A language identifier can be used to provide syntax highlighting.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

echo "Starting test execution"

./run_tests.sh \
  --suite regression \
  --log-level INFO \
  --output results/
```

The code is displayed in the document. It is not executed by Quarto.

## Option 3 — Captioned and Referenced Code

A code block can have a caption and identifier.

```yaml
test_execution:
  environment: test
  suite: regression
  retries: 3
  logging:
    level: INFO
    output: results/execution.log
```

: Example execution configuration {#lst-config}

Listing @lst-config demonstrates how a code block can be referenced from
normal document text.

# Mermaid Diagrams

The following diagrams use Quarto's Mermaid integration.

For DOCX output, the diagrams are intended to be rendered as **graphical
figures** and inserted into the generated Word document.

No Jupyter kernel is required.

## Example 1 — Flowchart

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-execution-flow
%%| fig-cap: "Test execution flow"
flowchart TD
    A[Start Test Execution] --> B[Load Configuration]
    B --> C[Initialize Environment]
    C --> D[Execute Tests]
    D --> E[Collect Results]
    E --> F[Generate Report]
    F --> G[Finish]
```

Figure @fig-execution-flow shows the overall execution flow.

## Example 2 — Sequence Diagram

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-execution-sequence
%%| fig-cap: "Test execution interaction sequence"
sequenceDiagram
    participant Runner
    participant DUT as Device Under Test
    participant Logger
    participant Reporter

    Runner->>DUT: Start test
    DUT-->>Runner: Test result
    Runner->>Logger: Write execution event
    Logger-->>Runner: Event stored
    Runner->>Reporter: Generate report
    Reporter-->>Runner: Report ready
```

Figure @fig-execution-sequence shows the interaction between the test
runner, device under test, logger, and reporting component.

## Example 3 — Entity Relationship Diagram

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-test-data-model
%%| fig-cap: "Logical test execution data model"
erDiagram
    TEST_RUN ||--o{ TEST_CASE : contains
    TEST_CASE ||--o{ TEST_RESULT : produces
    TEST_RUN ||--|| EXECUTION_ENVIRONMENT : uses

    TEST_RUN {
        string run_id
        datetime started_at
        string status
    }

    TEST_CASE {
        string test_id
        string name
        string suite
    }

    TEST_RESULT {
        string result_id
        string status
        string log_reference
    }

    EXECUTION_ENVIRONMENT {
        string environment_id
        string name
        string version
    }
```

Figure @fig-test-data-model demonstrates a logical data schema.

## Example 4 — State Diagram

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-test-state
%%| fig-cap: "Test run state lifecycle"
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Created
    Created --> Queued
    Queued --> Running

    Running --> Passed
    Running --> Failed
    Running --> Aborted

    Failed --> Retrying
    Retrying --> Running

    Passed --> Completed
    Aborted --> Completed
    Completed --> [*]
```

Figure @fig-test-state shows the lifecycle of an individual test run.

## Example 5 — Class Diagram

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-test-class-model
%%| fig-cap: "Test automation object model"
classDiagram
    class TestRun {
        +String runId
        +DateTime startedAt
        +String status
        +start()
        +finish()
    }

    class TestCase {
        +String testId
        +String name
        +execute()
    }

    class TestResult {
        +String status
        +String message
        +String logPath
    }

    TestRun "1" --> "*" TestCase : executes
    TestCase "1" --> "*" TestResult : produces
```

Figure @fig-test-class-model documents the main test automation objects and
their relationships.

# Mermaid and DOCX Rendering

The Mermaid blocks above are not ordinary code blocks. They are Quarto
diagram blocks:

```text
```{mermaid}
...
```
```

Quarto processes these diagrams during rendering.

For a DOCX target, the desired result is:

```text
QMD source
   |
   v
Quarto
   |
   +--> Mermaid source
   |
   v
Rendered diagram
   |
   v
Graphical figure
   |
   v
Microsoft Word DOCX
```

The Mermaid source therefore does not need to be supported natively by
Microsoft Word.

## Recommended Render Command

Render the document with:

```bash
quarto render quarto_docx_examples.qmd --to docx
```

The resulting `.docx` should contain the Mermaid diagrams as graphical
figures.
